revisions.summary: Nothing changed in the reading: it is the one approved before the blend took its place as the main reading.

The intention: The first drummer barely lifts his feet. The bright signal opens the stride, and each bass beat buys a little more time in the air. The pickup halfway through breaks that swing and the second run of beats starts building it again. The low D brings the rider down close enough to brush the words, then the returning beat carries him forward until the four short strokes catch up.

The intention: Make the bare drummer feel planted, with little words brushing past each beat. The bright signal opens a window above the track, then the low pulse takes off in a long, shallow run. The low singer breaks that run into slow arcs over the bare drums, leaving the last two vowels almost weightless. The returning kick pulls the rider back into stride. The roll folds into four short, low steps.

The intention: Slowed down, the low pulse becomes a heavy ball: once the bright signal has rung out, the rider bounces once per beat in round, unhurried arcs, slower than before, each landing an even weight so that the two big kicks (5.3 s and 14.2 s) stand out of the gait instead of being two among many. Before it, the bare drummer and words skitter low and quick, hard drum and feather word in turn. The lower singer then lets it drift, flatter and softer, until the return at 31.4 slams down and the rest runs low and driving, strong and light strokes alternating, into a roll that climbs. The approved reading rode everything at one fast pace with landings of many similar weights; this one gives each passage its own gait. Most visible in the bouncing pulse (5–22 s) against the drift after it.

The intention: Slowed down, the low pulse is a heavy ball, and the song is the story of how it gets rolling again. The bare drummer and his words keep the approved quick, even stride; the bright signal is one high float. From the first bass catch the rider bounces once per beat in round, unhurried arcs, every landing one of two weights so the two big kicks stand out of the gait: Opus's idea, the cleanest ride of the four here. The lower singer lets it drift lower and flatter, softer than the ball, as Opus and Sol had it. My own part: over the singer's last bar the rider gathers speed again, so the return at 31.4 lands with the weight the slowed readings lost there; from it on, the approved fast, low run with its own strengths and roll, which held the returning drums best of the four.
This is the blend, the main reading of the song since 2026-11-19. Nothing changed in it.
